chapter: Italy and the future of New Orleans jazz
title: Italian influence on jazz and garbled record talk
summary: Mazzari has heard no sign of Italian music in jazz; Allen then mentions Wingy Manone and record details whose names are garbled in the transcript.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Do you think any Italian music has gone into jazz? Do you hear any of it?

I don't know. I've heard hardly anything that would give you any sign of that. But of course, what you hear here is limited. Once I get over there, I might be able to form an opinion to that effect. But right now, I don't know.
Oh, Wingy swings out on us all on me. Oh, Wingy Manon.
Let's see. And the sax set from Lucia goes into... Kiodori did that. And blues for Jimmy on the Columbia record.
He had a Mordecai or Bodat on the bass, you know.
